summary: Tree crow's nest and shelter platform on Tire Mountain, Willamette NF, Lane County OR; register says destroyed 1950s. Sources disagree whether the crow's nest remains.

facts.design: Tree crow's nest (platform on a topped tree) with a three-sided shelter; Adirondack shelter added 1932, cabin 1936, per the register
facts.status_note: Register says the lookout was destroyed in the 1950s; it says the crow's nest is still standing, firelookout.com says still there, and Oregon Hikers says nothing remains
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Willamette National Forest

access.note: A side trail at the four-mile mark of Tire Mountain Trail #3485 gives access to the top; the trail is open to hikers, horses, mountain bikes and motorcycles. The Forest Service page says the area was affected by the Tire Mountain Fire.

visit.trail_note: Tire Mountain Trail #3485 is 6.1 miles (9.8 km); the side trail at the four-mile mark reaches the top. Check current conditions with the local ranger station.

events.note: Register and firelookout.com date the tree crow's nest to 'the 1920's'; the exact year is not given
December 4, 1925 newspaper item: the peak probably will be designated a fire lookout point after a supervisor and a ranger climbed it
Adirondack shelter constructed in 1932 (register); a 1932 item describes a 30-foot lookout tree set up as an emergency observation point
Register lists removal in the 1950's and says the lookout was destroyed in the 1950's; the year is approximate
Registered November 18, 2019; nominated by Tammy McLeod

corrections.why: Register lists the build as 'the 1920's' and firelookout.com says 'Developed in the 1920's'; no single year is stated

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Recorded as gone: the register says the lookout was destroyed in the 1950s and the Forest Service page describes it in the past tense. Whether the crow's nest platform still stands is disputed (register and firelookout.com say yes; Oregon Hikers says nothing remains) and is not resolved.

notes_for_editor: Brief said built 1920 and removed 1950; the register gives only 'the 1920's' and 'the 1950's'. Status conflict: register and firelookout.com say the crow's nest is still there; Oregon Hikers says nothing remains; FS trail page uses past tense. The 9.1 m height is the 1932 '30-foot lookout tree' figure, not a measured platform height. Tire Mountain Fire is named on the FS trail page with no date; no fire event recorded. Brief's 'Cascade National Forest' name appears only in the 1925 item, not used. Register photos (1930, 1934, 1938) have credits but no image URLs were captured, so none recorded. Staffing not documented in any source read.
